1	# Handoff — Fleet: adopting the `ai` namespace (lab-ai), 5 of 8 paths done
2	Written: 2026-07-29 23:01 · Session: 159 turns
3	
4	## Where things stand
5	
6	`lab-ai` is live on the Rancher controller with **5 of its 8 paths** — all five
7	raw-manifest ones, adopted one at a time, every BundleDeployment
8	`ready=true, nonModified=true`, verified as a true no-op. The **three Helm paths
9	(`04-ollama`, `05-open-webui`, `06-milvus`) are pre-flighted clean but NOT yet
10	added**; the user explicitly chose to pause before them.
11	
12	Work is committed as **`26a4af5` on branch `fleet-adopt-lab-ai-raw`** (branched off
13	content identical to `origin/main` @ `aa0ee88`). Tree clean. **Not pushed, no PR.**
14	
15	The full detail lives in the repo and is the real source of record — read
16	`14-cluster-mgmt/FLEET-WIRING.md` (adoption log entry for `lab-ai`, plus
17	Watch-outs) and `14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/README.md`. Don't re-derive from this
18	handoff what those files already say.
19	
20	## Decisions made (and why)
21	
22	**Deleted `14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/lab-ai.yaml` outright.** It listed all eight
23	paths, so a single `kubectl apply -f` would widen the GitRepo by every unadopted
24	path at once — exactly what the one-at-a-time rule exists to prevent. A file whose
25	whole convention is "apply me" cannot safely hold a staged rollout. The staging
26	now lives in `gitrepos/README.md` as patch commands. The GitRepo spec is
27	recoverable from any sibling file (they differ only in `name` and `paths`).
28	**Do not recreate this file** — the README says so explicitly.
29	
30	**Trimmed, not deleted, the other two multi-path files.** `lab-metallb-system.yaml`
31	and `lab-nvidia-device-plugin.yaml` each carried two paths. Each was reduced to its
32	safe *first* path, with the second documented as a patch command in the file's own
33	header comment. Unlike `lab-ai` (5 adopted + 3 pending, which no single file can
34	honestly represent), a 2-path file *is* expressible as "path one, then patch", so
35	it keeps its comments and stays applyable. Result: **all 8 remaining files hold
36	exactly one path** — the invariant is now uniform and stated as a rule in the
37	README ("never more than one unadopted path per file").
38	
39	**Adopted the render-based Helm pre-flight over the documented one.** The repo's
40	existing watch-out says to diff `helm get manifest <release>` against live. That
41	tests the *recorded release*, not what Fleet will apply. The right check is:
42	
43	    helm template <release> <repo>/<chart> --version <pinned> -n ai \
44	      -f <dir>/values.yaml --no-hooks > /tmp/render.yaml
45	    kubectl diff -n ai -f /tmp/render.yaml
46	
47	The two checks **disagree on open-webui**: the recorded release still says
48	`ollama:11434`, while the repo's values.yaml and live both say
49	`ollama-exporter:9401`. So `helm get manifest` shows a scary diff that the render
50	check proves is a no-op — adoption *closes* that drift rather than changing the
51	cluster. Going by the documented check alone would have stalled the path for
52	nothing. Both checks are now documented, with the render one marked as decisive.
53	
54	**Widen by patching `spec.paths`, never by re-applying a file.**
55	
56	## Files touched
57	
58	- `14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/lab-ai.yaml` — **deleted** (see above)
59	- `14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/README.md` — new sections: why `lab-ai` has no file +
60	  its patch/verify/rollback commands; the one-unadopted-path rule; the
61	  `03-gpu/runtimeclass` k3s-ownership problem. Table + status rows updated.
62	- `14-cluster-mgmt/FLEET-WIRING.md` — new `lab-ai` adoption-log entry with the
63	  before/after evidence table and the render-based pre-flight method; new
64	  watch-out for `03-gpu/runtimeclass`; the `helm get manifest` watch-out now
65	  explains what a diff there does and does not mean; "Next step" pointer added.
66	- `14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/lab-metallb-system.yaml` — trimmed to `01-networking`
67	- `14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/lab-nvidia-device-plugin.yaml` — trimmed to `03-gpu`,
68	  plus a long header comment on the k3s RuntimeClass hazard and the reversed
69	  stage order
70	
71	No manifests under `01-`…`13-` were touched. No cluster workload was modified
72	beyond Fleet taking Helm ownership of already-existing objects.
73	
74	## What's verified vs assumed
75	
76	**Verified by running it:**
77	- All 5 raw paths adopted; `ready=true, nonModified=true` on every one, first sync,
78	  no `ErrApplied`, no retries.
79	- No-op proven by a whole-namespace before/after snapshot diff: **zero** changes to
80	  any pod UID, startTime, or restart count, and none of the 46 ReplicaSets moved.
81	  Only movement was +1 `generation` on the 8 adopted Deployments (the documented
82	  inert bump) and 5 new Helm releases at revision 1.
83	- New finding: CronJob `generation` did **not** move at all — the inert bump hits
84	  Deployments only. This narrows the earlier node-red observation.
85	- `ollama-exporter` 9401 proxy live-probed post-adoption (open-webui depends on it):
86	  returned `{"version":"0.32.0"}`.
87	- All 10 raw manifests `kubectl diff`-clean before adoption. No hermes-style
88	  `env.value`/`valueFrom` trap anywhere in `ai`.
89	- All 3 Helm charts render **identically to live** with the repo's own values
90	  (`04-ollama` rel. 14, `05-open-webui` rel. 1, `06-milvus` rel. 1).
91	- Prereq Secrets `github-mcp-token` and `harbor-pull` exist in `ai`.
92	- All 8 remaining GitRepo files parse as valid GitRepos with the right
93	  `ash4d-lab: ""` selector, `branch: main`, `namespace: fleet-default`.
94	- The `04-ollama` widen patch was **server-dry-run** and produces exactly the
95	  intended 6-path list; live `spec.paths` confirmed still at 5 afterwards.
96	- The README's verify command was run verbatim and works.
97	
98	**Assumed / reasoned but NOT executed:**
99	- That the three Helm adoptions will be no-ops. Pre-flight strongly predicts it,
100	  but none has been applied.
101	- That Fleet won't create `ollama-test-connection` (a `helm.sh/hook: test` Pod that
102	  `helm template` emits). Reasoned from Helm semantics — test hooks run only on
103	  `helm test` — and the Pod is absent from live. Not observed under Fleet directly.
104	  Use `--no-hooks` when rendering so it doesn't read as a phantom addition.
105	- The `03-gpu/runtimeclass` k3s tug-of-war is **inferred from ownership
106	  annotations**, not tested. Nothing was adopted, so nothing broke.
107	
108	**Environment gotchas hit this session:** `kubectl diff -R -f <dir>` fails on the
109	bundle's own `fleet.yaml` (`Object 'Kind' is missing`) — exclude it with
110	`find <dir> -name '*.yaml' -not -name 'fleet.yaml'`. And zsh does not word-split
111	unquoted `$var`, which silently reduced a verification loop to one file per
112	directory; use `while IFS= read -r`.
113	
114	## Next step
115	
116	**Add `04-ollama` — and only `04-ollama` — to the live `lab-ai` GitRepo.** Pre-flight
117	is already done and clean; no need to redo it unless `main` has moved.
118	
119	    kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default patch gitrepo lab-ai --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"paths":[
120	      "08-indexer","09-mcp","07-comfyui","06-milvus/attu","04-ollama/ollama-exporter",
121	      "04-ollama"
122	    ]}}'
123	
124	Then confirm before going further:
125	
126	    kubectl --context rancher -n cluster-fleet-default-c-nnzn9-eaf6ebdbb298 \
127	      get bundledeployments -o custom-columns=\
128	    'NAME:.metadata.name,READY:.status.ready,NONMODIFIED:.status.nonModified' | grep lab-ai
129	
130	Spot-check that the `ollama` pod did not restart (it is the V100 holder) and that
131	`helm -n ai list` shows `ollama` still at revision 14 — Fleet adopting should not
132	bump it. Roll back by patching `spec.paths` without the entry just added.
133	
134	Queued behind that: `05-open-webui`, then `06-milvus`, same pattern. Then the
135	remaining namespaces in order — `lab-metallb-system`,
136	`lab-nvidia-device-plugin`, `lab-cattle-monitoring-system`, and
137	`lab-longhorn-system` **last** (its `defaultClassReplicaCount: 1` vs chart default
138	3 is the single most dangerous item in this whole effort).
139	
140	The session-scratchpad helpers (`addpath.sh`, `ai-before.txt`, chart renders) are
141	gone with the session — regenerate snapshots from the commands in the FLEET-WIRING
142	`lab-ai` log entry if needed.
143	
144	## Open questions
145	
146	1. **`03-gpu/runtimeclass` — does it belong in Fleet at all?** The live `nvidia` and
147	   `nvidia-experimental` RuntimeClasses are owned by k3s's bundled `runtimes`
148	   Addon (`objectset.rio.cattle.io/owner-gvk: k3s.cattle.io/v1, Kind=Addon`,
149	   `owner-name: runtimes`), as old as the cluster. Adopting the path aims Fleet and
150	   k3s's addon controller at the same cluster-scoped objects; if they fight, GPU
151	   scheduling breaks for ollama, comfyui and dcgm-exporter simultaneously. The
152	   committed manifest also has the `objectset.rio.cattle.io/*` annotations pasted
153	   in verbatim — a symptom of the same confusion. Assistant's read: leave these to
154	   k3s, like Traefik, and drop the path. **User has not decided.** Path is already
155	   removed from the GitRepo file pending that call.
156	2. **Push `fleet-adopt-lab-ai-raw` / open a PR?** Committed locally only. The user
157	   was asked and had not answered when the session ended.
158	3. **`correctDrift` stays off everywhere** until all namespaces are adopted and
159	   verified. Unchanged, just don't forget it.
160

content.text:
Read the handoff. **Nothing was actually broken** — and it's now cleared.

## What was wrong

The four repos weren't erroring in any way that affected the cluster. `Ready=True` on all of them, and all nine BundleDeployments were `ready=true, nonModified=true` throughout. The red status came from a **stale `Stalled` condition** about *polling for new commits*, not about applying them.

The timeline from the gitjob logs:
- 03:32:58Z — all four polled GitHub fine, picked up `aa0ee88`
- 03:36:36–03:36:49Z — all four failed within 13 seconds of each other
- then **no further poll for 28+ minutes**, until I forced a reconcile

`lab-ai` looked healthy only by accident: your `spec.paths` patches at 03:44–03:46 kept forcing it to reconcile, which re-polled and cleared its condition. Same blip hit it too.

The blip itself was transient. From inside the exact pod that does the polling, `git ls-remote` runs in 242–336 ms, five for five.

## The part that actually matters

`GITREPO_SYNC_PERIOD=2h` on the `gitjob` deployment. A polling failure doesn't retry on a short interval — recovery needs a new commit, a write to the object, or that 2-hour resync. And `status.webhookCommit` is empty on every repo, so there's no webhook; commit pickup depends entirely on polling. So a momentary GitHub hiccup can cost up to two hours of sync latency, silently. That's a real gap, not a cosmetic one.

## Fix applied

Cleared all four with a metadata-only annotation write, then removed the annotation. Verified harmless:
- generations unchanged (6/2/3/2/2, same as before)
- no Jobs created in `fleet-default`
- no pod restarts or `startTime` changes downstream

All five now `Ready/Accepted/GitPolling=True`, `Stalled=False`, commit `aa0ee88` = current `main`.

Recorded as a watch-out in `14-cluster-mgmt/FLEET-WIRING.md:187` — symptom, the "check BundleDeployments first" rule, the nudge command, and a warning against `fleet.cattle.io/force-update` (which *would* redeploy). Uncommitted, on `fleet-adopt-lab-ai-raw`.

Two things I did **not** do, since they're your call:

1. **Shorten `GITREPO_SYNC_PERIOD` or add a GitHub webhook.** Either would fix the 2h dormancy properly. But that deployment is Rancher-managed, so editing it directly will likely be reverted — it probably needs to go through the Rancher Fleet chart values. Worth deciding before you rely on Fleet for anything time-sensitive.
2. **Resumed the `04-ollama` adoption.** The handoff's next step is still pending and its pre-flight is still valid — `main` hasn't moved off `aa0ee88`.

Also still open from the handoff: the `03-gpu/runtimeclass` k3s-ownership decision, and whether to push `fleet-adopt-lab-ai-raw` / open a PR.

In ~/Developer there are several projects that should probably be moved to lab-fleet, even if it's just as a subvolume. ash4d.com, buzz-relay, lab-memory, nemoclaw-ops-agent, and ollama-code-mcp are the ones that stand out so far.

# lab-fleet — Home Lab Cluster Configuration as Code [![FOSSA Status](https://app.fossa.com/api/projects/git%2Bgithub.com%2Fdarthzen%2Flab-fleet.svg?type=shield)](https://app.fossa.com/projects/git%2Bgithub.com%2Fdarthzen%2Flab-fleet?ref=badge_shield) The complete, install-ordered configuration of a single-node k3s cluster running a private AI platform: local LLM inference on a Tesla V100, RAG over Milvus, agentic MCP tooling, GPU image generation, and the home services that share the node. Every file was curated from **live cluster state** — helm values pulled from running releases, manifests reconstructed from applied objects, and application sources recovered from container image layers after their Dockerfiles were lost. This repo is mounted as the [`lab/` submodule of ash4d.com](https://github.com/darthzen/ash4d.com), which carries the full architecture documentation. This repo carries the configs. ## Installation Order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph host["00 — Host (openSUSE Leap 16.0)"] DRIVER[NVIDIA G06 driver + CDI] K3S[k3s v1.35] end subgraph platform["01-03 — Platform"] METALLB[01 MetalLB

content.text:
I have the full picture. Two of your six premises change on inspection.

## The two that aren't what they look like

**`ollama-exporter` is already done.** It's Fleet-managed in the `ai` namespace right now — `04-ollama/ollama-exporter/ollama-exporter.yaml`, bundle `lab-ai-04-ollama-ollama-exporter`, `ready=true, nonModified=true`. It's one of the five paths you adopted last session. The `~/Developer/ollama-exporter` directory is the *Go source* for the image (goreleaser, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING, LICENSE, CI) — a standalone OSS project that shouldn't be absorbed. Nothing to move; it's already where you want it.

**`ash4d.com` is circular.** lab-fleet is already the `lab/` submodule *of* ash4d.com — confirmed in that repo's `.gitmodules`. Making ash4d.com a submodule of lab-fleet inverts an existing relationship. Its three `deploy/` manifests are just yaml and can come in freely; the *project* cannot. Also note the local `~/Developer/ash4d.com` has no `.git` at all — it's a detached working copy, so whatever's in it may already diverge from the GitHub repo.

## The pattern the repo already establishes

lab-fleet holds **cluster state, not application source**. `04-ollama/ollama-exporter/` is `fleet.yaml` + one manifest. `09-mcp/docs-rag/` is a manifest + README while the source sits in `~/Developer/docs-rag-mcp`. Source is vendored only where it's *orphaned* — `08-indexer/` carries `index_k8s_docs.py` because it was recovered from image layers and has nowhere else to live. There are no submodules in lab-fleet.

So "subvolume" is the wrong shape for all of these. Manifests-only is the shape that matches.

## What's actually in scope

| Project | Namespace | Live | Deploy method | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ollama-code-mcp | `ollama-code` | 1 deploy, svc, ing, cm | kustomize | small |
| ash4d.com (manifests) | `ash4d-origin` | 1 deploy, svc, ing, 2 cm | raw | small |
| nemoclaw-ops-agent | `nemoclaw` + `nemoclaw-sandboxes` | **no workloads** — RBAC, netpol, PVCs, secrets only | raw | medium, low risk |
| lab-memory | `lab-memory` | 4 deploy, 2 sts, cronjob, 4 ing | **Helm** `karakeep` rev 2 + raw | large |
| buzz-relay | `buzz` | 2 deploy, 2 sts, 6 svc, 4 pvc | **Helm** `buzz` rev 7 | large |

`buzz` and `lab-memory` are Helm, which your own watch-outs call "the real hazard" — both need the `helm template` render pre-flight from the `lab-ai` log entry. `nemoclaw` is the cheapest real win: pure RBAC/netpol/PVC scaffolding with nothing running, so adoption can't restart anything.

## On moving ollama-code-mcp to `ai`

Good news on mechanics: its manifests hardcode **no namespace**, and `09-mcp/fleet.yaml` already sets `defaultNamespace: ai`. So dropping them into `09-mcp/ollama-code/` puts them in `ai` with zero manifest edits.

Two things to be careful about:

1. **The namespace move is not a no-op**, so it breaks the adopt-first discipline. `mcp-ollama.ash4d.com` can't serve from two namespaces at once, and `mcp-ollama-ash4d-tls` is namespace-scoped so cert-manager must re-issue in `ai`. It's a cutover with a brief outage for anything pointed at that host. I'd adopt it in place first as `lab-ollama-code` (verified no-op), *then* do the namespace move as a separate tracked Fleet change you can roll back — rather than conflating a migration with an adoption.

2. **`09-mcp` is already an adopted path.** Adding a file there deploys on commit with no widen gate — you lose the one-at-a-time staging you built. So the move should land as its own path first, or you accept that `09-mcp` commits go live immediately.

## Also unmanaged, not on your list

Since you said "so far": `registry` (Harbor, 7 workloads, `registry.ash4d.com`), `cert-manager` (Helm, 3), `openshell` (Helm, 1), `agent-sandbox-system` (1), `managed-agent` (1), `trading-agent` (0 workloads — dormant). `registry` is notable because Harbor hosts the image `ollama-exporter` pulls, so it's load-bearing for an already-adopted path.

Two decisions gate the work: (a) confirm manifests-only rather than submodules, and (b) whether ollama-code-mcp gets adopted in place before the `ai` move or you'd rather just do the move by hand and adopt the result. I'd also suggest starting with `nemoclaw` regardless, since it's the one with no restart risk.

The `FLEET-WIRING.md` watch-out from the polling fix is still uncommitted, by the way.

The downtime is fine for all of these, unless they rely on each other. Just go ahead and do what needs to be done in one fell swoop.  Of your recommendations, trading-agent doesn't need to be implemented. It's not under active development and it isn't deployable. Nemoclaw probably should be added in as well.
Downtime authorized, `trading-agent` out, `nemoclaw` in. First I need to settle your one condition — cross-dependencies — because that determines what can be batched.

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Recover a full Helm chart source tree from a Helm v3 release secret.

The chart that produced a release is stored verbatim inside the release
secret, so a chart whose source has been lost is still recoverable from any
cluster still running it.

Secret .data.release is: base64 (k8s) -> base64 (helm) -> gzip -> JSON.
"""
import base64
import gzip
import json
import pathlib
import subprocess
import sys


def load_release(context, namespace, secret):
    raw = subprocess.run(
        ["kubectl", "--context", context, "-n", namespace,
         "get", "secret", secret, "-o", "jsonpath={.data.release}"],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
    ).stdout
    # k8s layer, then helm's own layer, then gzip
    blob = base64.b64decode(base64.b64decode(raw))
    return json.loads(gzip.decompress(blob))


def write_chart(chart, outdir, _depth=0):
    """Write Chart.yaml, values.yaml, templates/ and files/ for a chart
    and recurse into any vendored subcharts."""
    outdir = pathlib.Path(outdir)
    outdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    written = []

    meta = chart.get("metadata") or {}
    # Round-trip the metadata as YAML rather than re-serialising by hand.
    import yaml
    (outdir / "Chart.yaml").write_text(yaml.safe_dump(meta, sort_keys=False))
    written.append(outdir / "Chart.yaml")

    if chart.get("values"):
        (outdir / "values.yaml").write_text(
            yaml.safe_dump(chart["values"], sort_keys=False))
        written.append(outdir / "values.yaml")

    # templates[] and files[] both carry base64 data under .data
    for group in ("templates", "files"):
        for entry in chart.get(group) or []:
            name = entry["name"]
            # template names are already prefixed "templates/..."
            target = outdir / name
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target.write_bytes(base64.b64decode(entry["data"]))
            written.append(target)

    for sub in chart.get("dependencies") or []:
        subname = (sub.get("metadata") or {}).get("name", "subchart")
        written += write_chart(sub, outdir / "charts" / subname, _depth + 1)

    return written


def main():
    context, namespace, secret, outdir = sys.argv[1:5]
    rel = load_release(context, namespace, secret)
    chart = rel["chart"]
    meta = chart["metadata"]
    print(f"release {rel['name']} rev {rel['version']} status {rel['info']['status']}")
    print(f"chart   {meta.get('name')} {meta.get('version')} (app {meta.get('appVersion')})")

    written = write_chart(chart, outdir)
    print(f"wrote   {len(written)} files under {outdir}")

    # The values the user actually supplied, distinct from chart defaults.
    supplied = rel.get("config") or {}
    if supplied:
        import yaml
        p = pathlib.Path(outdir).parent / "values.yaml"
        p.write_text(
            "# Values as supplied to the live release, recovered from the\n"
            f"# Helm release secret ({namespace}/{secret}).\n"
            + yaml.safe_dump(supplied, sort_keys=False))
        print(f"wrote   supplied values -> {p}")
    else:
        print("note    release carries no user-supplied values (all chart defaults)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Split a rendered manifest stream by target namespace.

Objects with no explicit metadata.namespace inherit the release namespace,
so they are grouped under `default_ns`. Cluster-scoped kinds are grouped
separately since `kubectl diff -n` would mislabel them.
"""
import sys
import yaml

CLUSTER_SCOPED = {
    "ClusterRole", "ClusterRoleBinding", "CustomResourceDefinition",
    "Namespace", "ClusterIssuer", "RuntimeClass", "StorageClass",
    "ValidatingWebhookConfiguration", "MutatingWebhookConfiguration",
    "APIService", "PriorityClass", "IngressClass",
}


def main():
    src, default_ns, outprefix = sys.argv[1:4]
    docs = [d for d in yaml.safe_load_all(open(src)) if d]

    groups = {}
    for d in docs:
        kind = d.get("kind", "?")
        name = (d.get("metadata") or {}).get("name", "?")
        ns = (d.get("metadata") or {}).get("namespace")
        if kind in CLUSTER_SCOPED:
            key = "_cluster"
        else:
            key = ns or default_ns
        groups.setdefault(key, []).append(d)
        print(f"  {key:22s} {kind:24s} {name}")

    for key, sel in groups.items():
        path = f"{outprefix}-{key}.yaml"
        with open(path, "w") as fh:
            yaml.safe_dump_all(sel, fh)
        print(f"wrote {len(sel):3d} -> {path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Fleet bundle — NemoClaw ops-agent scaffolding (raw manifests).
#
# This bundle is scaffolding only: two Namespaces, two ServiceAccounts with
# their ClusterRoles/Bindings, the audit PVC, and the NetworkPolicy set.
# There are NO Deployments, StatefulSets or CronJobs here — the agent itself
# is not running yet. That makes this the lowest-risk adoption in the repo:
# there is no pod template to perturb, so it cannot restart anything.
# Adopt it first.
#
# Creates BOTH `nemoclaw` and `nemoclaw-sandboxes`. Those are two namespaces
# under one GitRepo, which departs from the one-GitRepo-per-namespace rule —
# deliberately, because `nemoclaw-sandboxes` is created by this bundle rather
# than being an independent concern.
#
# ORDERING CONSTRAINT: the openshell chart (20-openshell) renders a
# ServiceAccount, Role, RoleBinding and NetworkPolicy INTO nemoclaw-sandboxes.
# This bundle must be adopted before that one, or openshell has no namespace
# to write into. The two are not independently removable.
#
# The netpol set references namespaces `openshell`, `ai` and `kube-system` by
# label selector only. Those are ordinary selectors, not hard dependencies —
# the policies apply whether or not the target namespaces are Fleet-managed.
#
# Deliberately NOT vendored from the nemoclaw-ops-agent repo:
#   - deploy/audit/audit-record.schema.json — Fleet applies *.json as a
#     manifest, so a JSON Schema file in a bundle path breaks the whole
#     bundle with "Object 'Kind' is missing". It is app documentation and
#     belongs in its own repo.
#   - deploy/rbac/TESTS.md, deploy/README.md, deploy/openshell/ — docs and
#     the openshell values, which live in 20-openshell instead.
#   - build-plan/tools (a git submodule of darthzen/agent-build-tools) — build
#     tooling, not cluster state.
defaultNamespace: nemoclaw

# Raw-manifest bundle, but Fleet still deploys it via Helm internally — so
# adopting the objects that are already on the cluster needs takeOwnership.
# Without it the first sync fails: the live objects carry no
# meta.helm.sh/release-name annotation, and Helm refuses to touch resources it
# does not believe it owns. With it, adoption is metadata-only (Helm labels on
# the top-level objects), so no pod template changes and no restarts.
helm:
  takeOwnership: true

# Fleet bundle — Buzz relay (Helm, VENDORED chart).
#
# Nostr-based messaging relay at buzz.ash4d.com: one relay binary serving
# WebSocket + REST + web UI, backed by bundled PostgreSQL and Redis subcharts.
#
# The chart is vendored under ./chart rather than pulled from a repo, because
# chart buzz-0.1.6 is published NOWHERE reachable. It is not on any configured
# helm repo, not at oci://ghcr.io/block/buzz, and github.com/block/buzz is an
# unrelated audio-transcription desktop app despite what the chart's own
# `home:` URL claims. ./chart was recovered from the live Helm release secret
# (buzz/sh.helm.release.v1.buzz.v7), which stores the chart verbatim.
# Verified: `helm template` with values.yaml renders byte-identical to live.
#
# Two things had to be repaired in the recovered chart:
#   1. Helm rewrites a dependency's `name` to its alias when storing a chart,
#      so Chart.yaml came back claiming the postgres subchart is named
#      "postgresql". That disagreed with the recovered Chart.lock and no
#      dependency build was possible until it was set back to "postgres".
#   2. The subcharts themselves are NOT in the release secret. They are
#      re-fetched from oci://registry-1.docker.io/cloudpirates, pinned to the
#      exact versions the recovered Chart.lock records (postgres 0.19.5,
#      redis 0.30.3) rather than the upstream "0.19.x"/"0.30.x" ranges, so the
#      render reproduces live instead of drifting. The resulting
#      charts/*.tgz are committed — Fleet does not run `helm dependency build`.
#
# PREREQUISITE SECRET: `buzz-relay` must exist in the namespace before this
# path is enabled. values.yaml sets secrets.existingSecret, which suppresses
# the chart's own Secret; the Postgres and Redis subcharts still read
# postgres-password / redis-password from that same name. See the buzz-relay
# repo's secret.md for the full required key list.
#
# TLS: there is deliberately NO tls block and NO cert-manager Certificate for
# buzz.ash4d.com on this cluster. TLS terminates at a GCP edge proxy, and both
# clusters run a Cloudflare DNS-01 solver against the same zone — if both
# issued for this host they would race on the same _acme-challenge TXT record
# at renewal time, unattended. Exactly one cluster owns that cert and it is
# GCP. This is why buzz-ext-ash4d-tls is a hand-made Secret here rather than a
# cert-manager Certificate. Do not "fix" this by adding an issuer annotation.
#
# The image is pinned by digest, split across image.repository and image.tag
# because the chart's helper does printf "%s:%s". The current pin is a
# SECURITY floor, not just a version choice: it is the first build containing
# the nostr 0.44.6 bump for RUSTSEC-2026-0216 (NIP-44 remote DoS). Do not roll
# back below it — see the comments in values.yaml.
#
# NOT vendored from the buzz-relay repo: gcp-proxy.yaml and gcp-ollama.yaml.
# Those are applied to a DIFFERENT cluster (the GCP k3s instance), not this
# one, so they are not lab-fleet's cluster state.
defaultNamespace: buzz
helm:
  releaseName: buzz
  chart: ./chart
  valuesFiles:
    - values.yaml
  takeOwnership: true

# Fleet bundle — standalone MinIO backing buzz object storage (raw manifests).
#
# Separate path from ../ because 17-buzz is a Helm bundle and Fleet allows one
# chart per path — the same reason 04-ollama/ollama-exporter is split out from
# 04-ollama.
#
# The buzz chart's own bundled minio subchart is disabled
# (minio.enabled: false in ../values.yaml) because it is eval-only. This is
# the real object store; the relay reaches it at
# http://buzz-minio.buzz.svc.cluster.local:9000 with credentials from the
# buzz-relay Secret.
#
# The bucket-creation Job that shipped alongside these manifests is NOT part of
# this bundle — see buzz-minio-mkbucket.job.yaml.txt for why.
defaultNamespace: buzz

# Raw-manifest bundle, but Fleet still deploys it via Helm internally — so
# adopting the objects that are already on the cluster needs takeOwnership.
# Without it the first sync fails: the live objects carry no
# meta.helm.sh/release-name annotation, and Helm refuses to touch resources it
# does not believe it owns. With it, adoption is metadata-only (Helm labels on
# the top-level objects), so no pod template changes and no restarts.
helm:
  takeOwnership: true

# Fleet bundle — Karakeep, the lab-memory bookmark/RAG store (Helm).
#
# Chart pinned to 0.32.0, matching the running release, so Fleet adopts rather
# than upgrades. All the interesting decisions are in values.yaml — read its
# header before touching anything, especially the two Secret notes.
#
# THIS IS THE ONE ADOPTION IN THIS BATCH THAT RESTARTS A POD. The live
# StatefulSet carries OCR_USE_LLM as its FIRST env entry; the chart emits env
# alphabetically, so OCR_USE_LLM renders between NEXTAUTH_URL and
# OLLAMA_BASE_URL. Same variable, same value, different position — which is
# still a pod-template change, so the karakeep StatefulSet rolls once on
# adoption. Nothing is being reconfigured; the live object had simply been
# hand-edited outside Helm. Expect exactly one karakeep pod replacement and no
# change to karakeep-chrome or karakeep-meilesearch.
#
# PREREQUISITE SECRETS (both already exist; this bundle does NOT manage them,
# see values.yaml note 1):
#   karakeep              — NEXTAUTH_SECRET
#   karakeep-meilesearch  — MEILI_MASTER_KEY   (note the chart's spelling)
# If either is missing when this path is enabled, karakeep comes up without a
# session secret and Meilisearch rejects every query.
#
# The MCP servers, the ingest CronJob and the karakeep Certificate are raw
# manifests and live in ./raw — separate path, because Fleet allows one chart
# per path.
defaultNamespace: lab-memory
helm:
  releaseName: karakeep
  repo: https://karakeep-app.github.io/helm-charts
  chart: karakeep
  version: "0.32.0"
  valuesFiles:
    - values.yaml
  takeOwnership: true

# Fleet bundle — lab-memory MCP servers, ingest CronJob, Certificate (raw).
#
# Separate path from ../ because 18-lab-memory is a Helm bundle and Fleet
# allows one chart per path.
#
# Contents:
#   mcp-memory.*           — the lab-memory MCP server (mcp-memory.ash4d.com)
#   sme-salesengineer.yaml — two more MCP servers in one file, each with its
#                            own Service and Ingress
#   ingest-cronjob.yaml    — lab-memory-ingest
#   karakeep-certificate.yaml — the karakeep-ash4d-tls Certificate. The other
#                            three Certificates in this namespace are created
#                            by cert-manager's ingress-shim from the Ingress
#                            annotations, so they are not declared here.
#
# All of the above verified `kubectl diff`-clean against live before adoption.
#
# NOTE (2026-07-30, not caused by this bundle): the most recent
# lab-memory-ingest run failed — job lab-memory-ingest-29755875, Failed 0/1.
# Adoption does not fix or worsen that; the CronJob schedule and spec match
# live exactly. Worth investigating separately.
#
# The completed lab-memory-eval Job is deliberately excluded — see
# eval-job.yaml.txt.
#
# The lab-memory repo's deploy/namespace.yaml is also excluded: Fleet creates
# the namespace from defaultNamespace, and declaring a cluster-scoped Namespace
# in two sibling bundles would make them contend for it.
defaultNamespace: lab-memory

# Raw-manifest bundle, but Fleet still deploys it via Helm internally — so
# adopting the objects that are already on the cluster needs takeOwnership.
# Without it the first sync fails: the live objects carry no
# meta.helm.sh/release-name annotation, and Helm refuses to touch resources it
# does not believe it owns. With it, adoption is metadata-only (Helm labels on
# the top-level objects), so no pod template changes and no restarts.
helm:
  takeOwnership: true

# Fleet bundle — cert-manager (Helm).
#
# Pinned to v1.20.2, matching the running release, so Fleet adopts rather than
# upgrades.
#
# THIS IS THE MOST LOAD-BEARING BUNDLE IN THE REPO AFTER LONGHORN. It issues
# every TLS certificate in the cluster — 8 Certificates across ai, hermes,
# lab-memory, ollama-code and registry, all through the single cluster-scoped
# letsencrypt-dns ClusterIssuer in ./issuer. Break it and TLS fails everywhere,
# though not immediately: existing certs keep serving until renewal.
#
# BEFORE ADOPTING, read values.yaml. It carries two extraArgs that exist only
# on the live Deployment and NOT in the recorded release. Omitting them is a
# delayed, cluster-wide certificate outage rather than an immediate one.
#
# Adoption restarts the cert-manager controller pod exactly once. The rendered
# arg SET is identical to live, but the chart emits extraArgs before
# --max-concurrent-challenges while live has them after it. Order is still part
# of the pod template, so the Deployment rolls. Nothing is reconfigured.
# cert-manager is stateless and re-reconciles on start; in-flight Challenges
# are retried.
#
# CRDs are chart-managed (crds.enabled: true), so this bundle owns 6
# CustomResourceDefinitions. That is why it is adopted LAST despite platform
# components normally coming first: if Fleet ever prunes this bundle it takes
# the CRDs with it, and every Certificate, Issuer and Order object in the
# cluster goes too. Do not delete this GitRepo to "roll back" — remove the path
# instead, and never enable correctDrift here until everything else is stable.
#
# Numbered 15 rather than inserted before 01 because renumbering the existing
# 00-14 tree would invalidate every GitRepo path and doc reference in the repo.
# Install order and directory order diverge here; see README.md.
defaultNamespace: cert-manager
helm:
  releaseName: cert-manager
  repo: https://charts.jetstack.io
  chart: cert-manager
  version: "v1.20.2"
  valuesFiles:
    - values.yaml
  takeOwnership: true

# Fleet bundle — letsencrypt-dns ClusterIssuer (raw manifest).
#
# Separate path from ../ because 15-cert-manager is a Helm bundle and Fleet
# allows one chart per path.
#
# ORDERING: the ClusterIssuer is a cert-manager CRD instance, so the CRDs must
# exist before this applies. In practice they already do (the cluster has been
# issuing certs since June), but on a rebuild adopt ../ first.
#
# PREREQUISITE SECRET: cloudflare-api-token (key: api-token) in the
# cert-manager namespace — the Cloudflare API token for the DNS-01 solver. Not
# in this repo. Verified present 2026-07-30.
#
# Verified `kubectl diff`-clean against live before adoption.
defaultNamespace: cert-manager

# Raw-manifest bundle, but Fleet still deploys it via Helm internally — so
# adopting the objects that are already on the cluster needs takeOwnership.
# Without it the first sync fails: the live objects carry no
# meta.helm.sh/release-name annotation, and Helm refuses to touch resources it
# does not believe it owns. With it, adoption is metadata-only (Helm labels on
# the top-level objects), so no pod template changes and no restarts.
helm:
  takeOwnership: true

    solvers:

              name: cloudflare-api-token
              key: api-token

# Fleet bundle — ollama-code MCP server (raw manifests).
#
# Moved here from the standalone ollama-code-mcp repo, and MOVED NAMESPACE at
# the same time: it ran in its own `ollama-code` namespace and belongs in `ai`
# with the rest of the MCP layer and ollama-exporter.
#
# The manifests needed no edits — none of them hardcodes a namespace, so
# defaultNamespace below is what places them. Verified `kubectl diff`-clean
# against the live objects in `ollama-code` before the move, so the only change
# is placement.
#
# THIS IS THE ONE PATH IN THIS BATCH THAT IS NOT AN ADOPTION. It is a
# migration, and it takes mcp-ollama.ash4d.com down briefly:
#
#   - The host cannot serve from two namespaces at once. Traefik would see two
#     Ingresses claiming mcp-ollama.ash4d.com and the result is undefined, so
#     this is a cutover, not a parallel run.
#   - mcp-ollama-ash4d-tls is namespace-scoped. The Certificate in
#     `ollama-code` does not follow the Ingress; cert-manager's ingress-shim
#     issues a NEW one in `ai` from the cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer
#     annotation. That is a fresh DNS-01 round trip, so expect a minute or two
#     of TLS failure after cutover, longer if Cloudflare is slow.
#   - Anything configured to reach mcp-ollama.ash4d.com blips for that window.
#
# Order: delete the old namespace's Ingress FIRST, then enable this path, so the
# two Ingresses never coexist. Full sequence and rollback in FLEET-WIRING.md.
#
# NOT copied from the source repo: k8s/cert-manager-issuer.yaml. It declares the
# same cluster-scoped `letsencrypt-dns` ClusterIssuer that 15-cert-manager/issuer
# now owns, and two bundles declaring one cluster-scoped object would contend
# for it. k8s/kustomization.yaml is also dropped — Fleet reads the manifests
# directly and never invoked it.
#
# NESTING NOTE: this directory sits under 09-mcp, which is itself an adopted
# path. It carries its own fleet.yaml specifically so Fleet treats it as a
# separate bundle rather than folding it into lab-ai-09-mcp — the same reason
# 09-mcp/docs-rag, which has NO fleet.yaml, IS folded in. Confirm at adoption
# time that lab-ai-09-mcp's resource count did not change.
defaultNamespace: ai

# Raw-manifest bundle, but Fleet still deploys it via Helm internally — so
# adopting the objects that are already on the cluster needs takeOwnership.
# Without it the first sync fails: the live objects carry no
# meta.helm.sh/release-name annotation, and Helm refuses to touch resources it
# does not believe it owns. With it, adoption is metadata-only (Helm labels on
# the top-level objects), so no pod template changes and no restarts.

  takeOwnership: true

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the new Fleet GitRepo files, matching the existing files' shape.

The boilerplate (what a GitRepo is, where it lives, the cluster selector
rationale, correctDrift) is identical across every file in gitrepos/ and is
reproduced verbatim so the new files read as siblings of the old ones.
"""
import pathlib

OUT = pathlib.Path("14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos")

HEADER = """# Fleet GitRepo — {ns} namespace.
#
# This is the Fleet `GitRepo` CUSTOM RESOURCE (gitrepos.fleet.cattle.io), not a
# git repository: it points Fleet at the existing lab-fleet repo and tells it
# which paths to render. It lives on the RANCHER CONTROLLER
# (192.168.7.148, kubectl context `rancher`), so it is not part of any bundle here.
#
#   kubectl --context rancher apply -f 14-cluster-mgmt/gitrepos/{name}.yaml
#
# One GitRepo per namespace — see gitrepos/README.md.
#
{notes}"""

BODY = """apiVersion: fleet.cattle.io/v1alpha1
kind: GitRepo
metadata:
  name: {name}
  namespace: fleet-default
spec:
  repo: https://github.com/darthzen/lab-fleet
  branch: main
  paths:
    - {path}
  # `ash4d-lab` is a bespoke label already on the sdf1 cluster (c-nnzn9). Chosen
  # over management.cattle.io/cluster-name, which Rancher owns and may rewrite.
  # Do NOT reuse site=ash4d — that belongs to the ash4d-site GitRepo and resolves
  # to a different downstream cluster.
  targets:
    - clusterSelector:
        matchLabels:
          ash4d-lab: ""
  # correctDrift OFF until every namespace is adopted and verified. Turning it on
  # makes Fleet revert out-of-band `kubectl edit`s — the eventual goal, but it
  # will fight this cluster's hand-tuning habits (GPU pins, context sizes).
  correctDrift:
    enabled: false
"""


def staged(name, first, second):
    """The standard note for a file whose namespace has a second path pending."""
    return (
        f"# STAGED: this file carries ONLY `{first}`, so applying it is a single\n"
        f"# adoption step and stays idempotent. `{second}` is deliberately left\n"
        "# out — see gitrepos/README.md on why a GitRepo file must never hold more\n"
        "# than one unadopted path. Add the second path after the first is verified\n"
        "# Ready:\n"
        "#\n"
        f"#   kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default patch gitrepo {name} \\\n"
        f"#     --type=merge -p '{{\"spec\":{{\"paths\":[\"{first}\",\"{second}\"]}}}}'\n"
    )


REPOS = [
    dict(
        name="lab-cert-manager", ns="cert-manager", path="15-cert-manager",
        notes=(
            "# HIGHEST RISK IN THIS BATCH, and the reason it is adopted LAST despite\n"
            "# being a platform component. It issues every TLS certificate in the\n"
            "# cluster (8 Certificates across ai, hermes, lab-memory, ollama-code,\n"
            "# registry) and this bundle OWNS the 6 cert-manager CRDs. Deleting this\n"
            "# GitRepo would delete the CRDs and with them every Certificate, Issuer\n"
            "# and Order in the cluster. Roll back by removing the path, never by\n"
            "# deleting the GitRepo.\n"
            "#\n"
            "# Adoption restarts the cert-manager controller pod once (arg ORDER\n"
            "# differs; the arg set is identical). Read 15-cert-manager/values.yaml\n"
            "# first — it carries two DNS-01 flags that exist only on the live object,\n"
            "# and adopting without them is a delayed cluster-wide cert outage.\n"
            "#\n"
            "# PREREQUISITE SECRET: cloudflare-api-token in the cert-manager namespace.\n"
            "#\n"
            + staged("lab-cert-manager", "15-cert-manager", "15-cert-manager/issuer")
        ),
    ),
    dict(
        name="lab-ash4d-origin", ns="ash4d-origin", path="16-ash4d-origin",
        notes=(
            "# LOW RISK: one nginx Deployment serving static HTML from a ConfigMap,\n"
            "# behind origin.ash4d.com. No TLS, no Secret prerequisites, no PVCs.\n"
            "# Verified `kubectl diff`-clean — a true no-op.\n"
            "#\n"
            "# Reconstructed from LIVE state, not from the ash4d.com repo's deploy/\n"
            "# directory. That directory targets the GCP cluster (namespace `ash4d`,\n"
            "# which does not exist here) and sets ingressClassName: nginx on a Traefik\n"
            "# cluster. See 16-ash4d-origin/fleet.yaml.\n"
            "#\n"
            "# Single path — nothing staged.\n"
        ),
    ),
    dict(
        name="lab-buzz", ns="buzz", path="17-buzz",
        notes=(
            "# MED RISK: stateful. 2 Deployments, 2 StatefulSets (bundled Postgres and\n"
            "# Redis) and 4 Longhorn PVCs. The chart is VENDORED because buzz-0.1.6 is\n"
            "# published nowhere reachable; it was recovered from the live Helm release\n"
            "# secret. Verified: renders byte-identical to live, so adoption is a no-op.\n"
            "#\n"
            "# PREREQUISITE SECRET: `buzz-relay` — the relay and BOTH subcharts read it.\n"
            "#\n"
            "# Do not add a cert-manager annotation for buzz.ash4d.com. TLS terminates\n"
            "# at a GCP edge proxy, and two clusters issuing for the same host would\n"
            "# race on the same _acme-challenge TXT record at renewal. See\n"
            "# 17-buzz/fleet.yaml.\n"
            "#\n"
            + staged("lab-buzz", "17-buzz", "17-buzz/minio")
        ),
    ),
    dict(
        name="lab-lab-memory", ns="lab-memory", path="18-lab-memory",
        notes=(
            "# NAME: the namespace really is `lab-memory`, so `lab-<namespace>` gives\n"
            "# the doubled `lab-lab-memory`. Kept rather than special-cased, so the\n"
            "# naming rule stays mechanical.\n"
            "#\n"
            "# MED RISK, and THE ONE ADOPTION IN THIS BATCH THAT RESTARTS A POD: the\n"
            "# karakeep StatefulSet rolls once because the live object carries\n"
            "# OCR_USE_LLM first while the chart emits env alphabetically. Same\n"
            "# variable, same value, different position. Nothing is reconfigured.\n"
            "#\n"
            "# PREREQUISITE SECRETS: `karakeep` and `karakeep-meilesearch` (note the\n"
            "# chart's spelling). 18-lab-memory/values.yaml disables the chart's own\n"
            "# Secret objects on purpose — leaving them enabled would ROTATE\n"
            "# NEXTAUTH_SECRET and MEILI_MASTER_KEY on first sync.\n"
            "#\n"
            + staged("lab-lab-memory", "18-lab-memory", "18-lab-memory/raw")
        ),
    ),
    dict(
        name="lab-nemoclaw", ns="nemoclaw", path="19-nemoclaw",
        notes=(
            "# LOWEST RISK IN THE WHOLE REPO — adopt this one FIRST. The bundle is\n"
            "# Namespaces, ServiceAccounts, RBAC, NetworkPolicies and one PVC. There\n"
            "# are no Deployments, StatefulSets or CronJobs, so there is no pod\n"
            "# template to perturb and nothing can restart. Verified\n"
            "# `kubectl diff`-clean across the whole bundle.\n"
            "#\n"
            "# COVERS TWO NAMESPACES (`nemoclaw` and `nemoclaw-sandboxes`), departing\n"
            "# from one-GitRepo-per-namespace on purpose: this bundle CREATES\n"
            "# nemoclaw-sandboxes, so it is not an independent concern.\n"
            "#\n"
            "# Must be adopted BEFORE lab-openshell, whose chart renders four objects\n"
            "# into nemoclaw-sandboxes.\n"
            "#\n"
            "# Single path — nothing staged.\n"
        ),
    ),
    dict(
        name="lab-openshell", ns="openshell", path="20-openshell",
        notes=(
            "# MED RISK. The chart is VENDORED, and that is not a stylistic choice:\n"
            "# upstream publishes only the MUTABLE tag `0.0.0-dev`, which has ALREADY\n"
            "# drifted from the running release. Pinning that tag would silently\n"
            "# upgrade openshell instead of adopting it. See 20-openshell/fleet.yaml.\n"
            "# Verified: the vendored chart renders identically to live.\n"
            "#\n"
            "# ADOPT AFTER lab-nemoclaw. This chart writes a ServiceAccount, Role,\n"
            "# RoleBinding and NetworkPolicy into the `nemoclaw-sandboxes` namespace,\n"
            "# which lab-nemoclaw creates. It also owns a cluster-scoped\n"
            "# ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding pair (openshell-node-reader).\n"
            "#\n"
            "# values.yaml came from the live release, NOT from the nemoclaw-ops-agent\n"
            "# repo's deploy/openshell/values.yaml — those disagree on\n"
            "# sandboxNamespace and the repo copy is stale.\n"
            "#\n"
            "# Single path — nothing staged.\n"
        ),
    ),
]

for r in REPOS:
    text = HEADER.format(**r) + BODY.format(**r)
    (OUT / f"{r['name']}.yaml").write_text(text)
    print(f"  wrote {OUT / (r['name'] + '.yaml')}")

input.new_string:
- **cert-manager's DNS-01 flags exist only on the live object — omitting them
  is a delayed, cluster-wide certificate outage.** The live `cert-manager`
  Deployment carries two args the chart does not render:

      --dns01-recursive-nameservers=1.1.1.1:53,8.8.8.8:53
      --dns01-recursive-nameservers-only

  Without them cert-manager runs its DNS-01 self-check against the cluster's own
  resolver, which does not serve the public view of `ash4d.com`. It would never
  observe the `_acme-challenge` TXT record it had just written, so every
  Challenge would sit pending until it timed out. **Nothing breaks at adoption
  time** — existing certs serve until renewal — which is what makes this
  dangerous: it surfaces weeks later as certs expiring on every ash4d.com
  hostname at once. Now captured as `extraArgs` in `15-cert-manager/values.yaml`.
  Same class as Longhorn's replica count: a value that exists only on the live
  object, invisible until much later.

- **A mutable chart tag is not a pin — `helm template` it before trusting it.**
  OpenShell is published only as `0.0.0-dev`, and that tag had *already* drifted
  from the running release: pulling it on 2026-07-30 yielded an added
  `server.workspaceStorageClass` value, added supervisor sidecar-topology
  options, and a rewritten `_helpers.tpl`. Writing `version: "0.0.0-dev"` the
  way `04-ollama` writes `version: "1.67.0"` looks identical but is not — it
  would have silently *upgraded* openshell under the guise of adopting it. When
  upstream offers no immutable version, vendor the chart. See
  `20-openshell/fleet.yaml`.

- **A lost chart is recoverable from the cluster running it.** Helm stores the
  chart verbatim inside the release Secret, so `buzz-0.1.6` and openshell's
  chart were both reconstructed from `sh.helm.release.v1.<rel>.v<n>` after their
  sources turned out to exist nowhere on disk or on GitHub. Two traps when doing
  this:
  - Helm rewrites a dependency's `name` to its **alias** when storing a chart,
    so the recovered `Chart.yaml` disagreed with the recovered `Chart.lock`
    (`postgresql` vs `postgres`) and no `helm dependency build` was possible
    until it was set back.
  - Subcharts are **not** in the release Secret. Re-fetch them pinned to the
    exact versions the recovered `Chart.lock` records, not the `0.19.x`-style
    ranges the chart declares, or the render drifts. Commit the resulting
    `charts/*.tgz` — Fleet does not run `helm dependency build`.

- **Jobs do not belong in a Fleet bundle.** A `Job` spec is near-immutable, so a
  Job inside a synced path makes Fleet fight the API server on every subsequent
  change, and a Job that has already completed and been reaped reads as a
  *creation* rather than a no-op. Three were split out and renamed `.yaml.txt`
  so Fleet never applies them, following the
  `09-mcp/github-mcp-token.secret.example.yaml.txt` convention:
  `17-buzz/minio/buzz-minio-mkbucket.job.yaml.txt` and
  `18-lab-memory/raw/eval-job.yaml.txt`.

- **Fleet applies `*.json` too.** `nemoclaw-ops-agent/deploy/audit/` ships an
  `audit-record.schema.json` next to its manifests; vendoring the directory
  wholesale would break the bundle with `Object 'Kind' is missing`. This is the
  same failure the `fleet.yaml` gotcha produces under `kubectl diff`, but here it
  breaks the real sync, not just a pre-flight. Vendor manifests, not directories.

### Directory numbers 15+ are append-order, not install-order

`15`–`20` were added after the original `00`–`14` tree and are numbered in the
order they were adopted, not their true position in a dependency graph.
**cert-manager (15) actually installs before almost everything** — it issues the
TLS for `attu` (06), `hermes` (10), `lab-memory` (18) and `registry`, so on a
rebuild it belongs alongside `01`–`03`. It was appended rather than inserted
because renumbering the existing tree would invalidate every Fleet `GitRepo`
path and every cross-reference in the docs, for a cosmetic gain.

Real dependency order for the new components:

    15-cert-manager  →  16, 17, 18   (anything terminating TLS in-cluster)
    19-nemoclaw      →  20-openshell (openshell writes into nemoclaw-sandboxes)

Two of these charts are **vendored** (committed under `<dir>/chart/`) rather than
pulled from a repo, which is a departure from `04`/`05`/`06`. Neither is
available to pin: `buzz-0.1.6` is published nowhere reachable, and OpenShell
publishes only the mutable tag `0.0.0-dev`, which has already drifted from what
is running. Both were recovered from their live Helm release Secrets. See
`14-cluster-mgmt/FLEET-WIRING.md`.

claiming `mcp-ollama.ash4d.com` and the winner is undefined; and
`mcp-ollama-ash4d-tls` is namespace-scoped, so the Certificate does not follow
the Ingress — cert-manager's ingress-shim has to issue a fresh one in `ai` from
the `cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer` annotation, which is a full DNS-01 round
trip.

Pre-flight already done: the repo manifests are `kubectl diff`-clean against the
live objects in `ollama-code`, so placement is the only thing changing. None of
them hardcodes a namespace, so `defaultNamespace: ai` is what moves it.

    # 1. Remove the old Ingress FIRST so the host is never claimed twice.
    kubectl --context sdf1 -n ollama-code delete ingress ollama-code-mcp

    # 2. Add the path to lab-ai (see gitrepos/README.md for the full list).
    kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default patch gitrepo lab-ai --type=merge \
      -p '{"spec":{"paths":["08-indexer","09-mcp","07-comfyui","06-milvus/attu","04-ollama/ollama-exporter","09-mcp/ollama-code"]}}'

    # 3. Confirm the new bundle is Ready, and that lab-ai-09-mcp did NOT change
    #    resource count (proving the nested fleet.yaml split it into its own bundle).
    kubectl --context rancher -n cluster-fleet-default-c-nnzn9-eaf6ebdbb298 \
      get bundledeployments -o custom-columns=\
    'NAME:.metadata.name,READY:.status.ready,NONMODIFIED:.status.nonModified' | grep lab-ai

    # 4. Wait for the new Certificate to go Ready in ai (DNS-01, allow a few minutes).
    kubectl --context sdf1 -n ai get certificate mcp-ollama-ash4d-tls -w

    # 5. Only once step 4 is Ready, retire the old namespace.
    kubectl --context sdf1 delete namespace ollama-code

**Rollback** (before step 5, which is the point of no return): remove
`09-mcp/ollama-code` from `spec.paths`, then re-apply the original manifests into
`ollama-code` from the `ollama-code-mcp` repo (`kubectl apply -n ollama-code -k
k8s/`). The old namespace still holds its own Certificate until step 5, so
rollback before then costs only another DNS-01 round trip.

Do not vendor `k8s/cert-manager-issuer.yaml` from that repo — it declares the
same cluster-scoped `letsencrypt-dns` ClusterIssuer that `15-cert-manager/issuer`
owns, and two bundles declaring one cluster-scoped object contend for it.

| `15-cert-manager/issuer` | ollama-code-mcp repo | `kubectl diff` clean |
| `16-ash4d-origin` | (live state) | `kubectl diff` clean — true no-op |

| `20-openshell` | release Secret | renders identically to live, all 3 groups |
| `09-mcp/ollama-code` | ollama-code-mcp repo | clean in place; **migration**, see runbook |

Four repo-vs-live drifts were found and resolved in the repo's favour of *live*,
because adoption must not change a running cluster:

1. **cert-manager** — two DNS-01 args on the live Deployment, in no chart value.
   Would have been a delayed cluster-wide cert outage. See Watch-outs.
2. **karakeep `OLLAMA_BASE_URL`** — recorded release said
   `http://192.168.7.153:11434`, live object said
   `ollama-exporter.ai.svc.cluster.local:9401`. Identical shape to the
   open-webui drift; live wins.
3. **karakeep secrets** — the chart regenerates `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` and
   `MEILI_MASTER_KEY` unless pinned, and the live values came from a git-ignored
   file. Chart-managed Secrets disabled instead; both are now prerequisites.
4. **openshell `sandboxNamespace`** — the nemoclaw repo's values say `nemoclaw`,
   live says `nemoclaw-sandboxes`. The repo copy is stale and would have moved
   the sandbox namespace out from under its own NetworkPolicy and RBAC.

Deliberately **excluded** from the repo, with reasons:

- **`registry` (Harbor).** Its objects carry `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=Helm`
  but there is **no release Secret and no `meta.helm.sh/release-name`
  annotation** — Helm-labelled and ownerless, so the chart cannot be recovered
  the way buzz and openshell were, and no values source survives. It is also
  load-bearing: it serves the `ollama-exporter` image that the already-adopted
  `04-ollama/ollama-exporter` path pulls. Needs its own session.
- **`agent-sandbox-system`** — upstream
  `registry.k8s.io/agent-sandbox/agent-sandbox-controller:v0.5.0`, third-party,
  no source in `~/Developer`, no ownership markers.
- **`managed-agent`** — a single `registry.suse.com/bci/python:3.12` worker with
  no ownership markers and no identifiable source. Looks like a scratch
  experiment; identify it before adopting.
- **`trading-agent`** — 0 workloads, not deployable, not under active
  development. Excluded at the user's direction.
- **`ollama-exporter`** — already Fleet-managed as `04-ollama/ollama-exporter`.
  The `~/Developer/ollama-exporter` directory is the Go source for the image (its
  own OSS project, with goreleaser/CHANGELOG/LICENSE) and does not belong here.
- **`ash4d.com` the project** — this repo is already ash4d.com's `lab/`
  submodule, so vendoring it back would be circular. Only its manifests could
  come in, and its `deploy/` directory turned out to target the **GCP** cluster
  (namespace `ash4d`, absent here; `ingressClassName: nginx` on a Traefik
  cluster), so `16-ash4d-origin` was reconstructed from live instead.

Guiding rule confirmed by all of the above: **lab-fleet holds cluster state, not
application source.** Projects with their own repo keep it; only their manifests
land here. Source is vendored only when it is orphaned (`08-indexer`) or when a
chart exists nowhere else (`17-buzz`, `20-openshell`).

Adds Fleet bundles for six namespaces that were running unmanaged, plus the
ollama-code MCP server relocated out of its own namespace into `ai`.

All ten paths are pre-flighted against the live cluster. **Nothing is adopted by
this PR** — no GitRepo has been applied. Merging makes the manifests available on
`main`; adoption is a separate, staged step per `gitrepos/README.md`.

| Path | Pre-flight |
|---|---|
| `15-cert-manager` (+ `/issuer`) | clean **after** adding two DNS-01 `extraArgs`; restarts controller once |
| `16-ash4d-origin` | `kubectl diff` clean — true no-op |
| `17-buzz` (+ `/minio`) | renders **byte-identical** to live |
| `18-lab-memory` (+ `/raw`) | clean **after** two drift fixes; rolls karakeep once |
| `19-nemoclaw` | clean — no pod templates at all, cannot restart anything |
| `20-openshell` | renders identically to live across all three groups |
| `09-mcp/ollama-code` | clean in place; **namespace migration**, brief outage |

## Two charts recovered from live Helm release secrets

Neither had a usable source. A Helm release stores its chart verbatim, so both
were reconstructed from `sh.helm.release.v1.<rel>.v<n>`:

- **`buzz-0.1.6`** is published nowhere reachable — not on any configured repo,
  and `github.com/block/buzz` is an unrelated audio-transcription app despite
  the chart's `home:` URL. Two traps: Helm rewrites a dependency's `name` to its
  alias when storing a chart (so `Chart.yaml` disagreed with `Chart.lock` until
  `postgresql` → `postgres` was undone), and subcharts are *not* in the release
  secret, so they are re-fetched pinned to the exact locked versions.
- **`openshell`** publishes only the mutable tag `0.0.0-dev`, which has
  **already drifted** from the running release. Pinning it the way `04-ollama`
  pins `1.67.0` would have silently *upgraded* openshell while looking like an
  adoption.

## Four repo-vs-live drifts, resolved in favour of live

1. **cert-manager** — two DNS-01 args exist only on the live Deployment. Their
   absence breaks nothing at adoption time and then fails every certificate
   renewal weeks later, across all ash4d.com hostnames at once.
2. **karakeep `OLLAMA_BASE_URL`** — recorded release said `192.168.7.153:11434`,
   live object said `ollama-exporter:9401`. Same shape as the known open-webui
   drift.
3. **karakeep secrets** — the chart regenerates `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` and
   `MEILI_MASTER_KEY` unless pinned, and the live values came from a git-ignored
   file. Chart-managed Secrets are disabled; both are documented prerequisites
   rather than committed values (this repo is public).
4. **openshell `sandboxNamespace`** — the nemoclaw repo's values are stale and
   would have moved sandboxes out from under their own NetworkPolicy and RBAC.

## Excluded, with reasons in FLEET-WIRING.md

`registry`/Harbor (Helm-labelled but **ownerless** — no release secret, so
nothing to recover, and it serves the image an already-adopted path pulls),
`agent-sandbox-system` and `managed-agent` (third-party / unidentified),
`trading-agent` (not deployable), `ollama-exporter` (already adopted), and
ash4d.com the project (this repo is already its `lab/` submodule, and its
`deploy/` targets the GCP cluster).

Guiding rule: **lab-fleet holds cluster state, not application source.**

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

content.text: Now the critical doc corrections — the rollback advice in this repo is actively dangerous, as I just proved:

input.old_string: - **cert-manager's DNS-01 flags exist only on the live object — omitting them
input.new_string:
- **🔴 "Roll back by removing the path" DESTROYS an adopted Helm release.
  Learned the hard way on 2026-07-30 — it deleted karakeep.** Removing a path
  from `spec.paths` deletes that bundle, and deleting a bundle whose Helm release
  Fleet has taken ownership of **uninstalls the release**. That is fine for a
  bundle still stuck in `WaitApplied` that never got ownership, and fine for raw
  bundles Fleet created itself. It is NOT fine once `takeOwnership` has
  succeeded: Fleet becomes the release owner, and removing the path runs the
  equivalent of `helm uninstall`.

  What it cost: karakeep's StatefulSets, its chrome Deployment, its Service and
  Ingress, and the `karakeep-meilesearch` PVC were all deleted. Recovery was a
  plain `helm upgrade --install` with this repo's own values.

  What survived, and why it matters:
  - `data-karakeep-0` — a StatefulSet `volumeClaimTemplates` PVC. Kubernetes
    does not garbage-collect these when the StatefulSet goes, so the primary
    data volume was still `Bound` and the reinstalled StatefulSet re-bound the
    same Longhorn volume by name.
  - `karakeep` and `karakeep-meilesearch` Secrets — untouched **only because**
    `18-lab-memory/values.yaml` had disabled the chart's Secret objects. Had
    they been chart-managed, the uninstall would have deleted both credentials.
  - The `karakeep-meilesearch` PVC did NOT survive: a plain subchart PVC is
    Helm-owned, so it was deleted. Meilisearch is a rebuildable index, so this
    cost a reindex rather than data.

  **Safe rollback for a bundle that reached ownership:** do not touch
  `spec.paths`. Either leave it and fix forward, or `spec.paused: true` to stop
  Fleet acting while you work. If the path must go, `helm uninstall` is what you
  are actually authorising — take a backup first.

- **`kubectl diff` clean does NOT mean Fleet will apply cleanly.** This is the
  pre-flight gap that caused the incident above. Fleet applies server-side, so
  it needs *field ownership*, not just matching values. karakeep failed with:

      Apply failed with 6 conflicts: conflicts with "helm":
      - .spec.template.spec.hostIPC
      - .spec.volumeClaimTemplates
      - .spec.template.spec.containers[name="karakeep"].resources.limits.cpu

  The values were semantically identical — live had `cpu: 1` where the chart
  renders `1000m`, and live simply omitted `hostIPC/hostNetwork/hostPID` where
  the chart renders explicit `false`. `kubectl diff` normalises all of that and
  reports clean. Server-side apply does not: it sees another manager (`helm`,
  from the original client-side-apply install) owning those paths and refuses.

  Neither escape is free. `helm.force: true` replaces objects, and
  `.spec.volumeClaimTemplates` is immutable, so on a StatefulSet that risks a
  delete/recreate of the data volume. Stripping the stale `helm` entry from
  `managedFields` lets Fleet take over but then it *writes* its normalised
  values, rolling the pod.

  So: add an ownership pre-flight before adopting any Helm release that predates
  Fleet. `kubectl apply --server-side --dry-run=server` against the render will
  surface the conflicts that `kubectl diff` hides.

- **A nested path with its own `fleet.yaml` deploys as soon as its PARENT path
  is adopted — it is not a staging gate.** Fleet scans the parent path
  recursively; a nested `fleet.yaml` splits that subdirectory into its own
  *bundle*, but it is still rendered and applied under the parent's path entry.
  Observed three times on 2026-07-30: adopting `09-mcp` immediately deployed
  `09-mcp/ollama-code`, `17-buzz` brought `17-buzz/minio`, and `18-lab-memory`
  brought `18-lab-memory/raw` — none of which were in `spec.paths`.

  Consequence: the "apply the first path, then patch in the second" staging
  pattern **does not work for nested paths**. It only works for siblings, the way
  `01-networking` and `01-networking/pools` are siblings. If a second path must
  be genuinely gated, make it a sibling directory, not a child.

- **A field the API server silently discards makes a bundle permanently
  `Modified`.** The buzz redis subchart sets
  `updateStrategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable: 1`, but this cluster has
  `MaxUnavailableStatefulSet` disabled (`kubernetes_feature_enabled{...} 0`), so
  the API server strips it on every apply. Fleet re-renders it, never sees it
  land, and reports `Modified` forever with no path to convergence — which hides
  real drift behind permanent noise. Fixed by nulling the value in
  `17-buzz/values.yaml`. Confirm suspicions with
  `kubectl patch --dry-run=server` and check whether the field comes back.

- **cert-manager's DNS-01 flags exist only on the live object — omitting them

and was destroyed and restored; cert-manager deliberately held.**

Live state after this session — every BundleDeployment `ready=true`:

| GitRepo | Paths live | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `lab-nemoclaw` | `19-nemoclaw` | ✅ `nonModified=true` first sync. Zero restarts, as predicted |

server-side-apply field-manager conflicts (see Watch-outs) — `kubectl diff` had
been clean, which is exactly the gap. Fleet retry-looped the release from rev 2
to rev 18, all `failed`, while the workload stayed healthy and untouched. To stop
the loop, `spec.paths` was narrowed to `18-lab-memory/raw`. **That uninstalled
the release**, deleting karakeep's two StatefulSets, its chrome Deployment,
Service, Ingress, and the `karakeep-meilesearch` PVC.

Restored with `helm upgrade --install karakeep karakeep-app/karakeep --version
0.32.0 -n lab-memory -f 18-lab-memory/values.yaml`. Outcome:

- **Primary data intact.** `data-karakeep-0` is a `volumeClaimTemplates` PVC,
  which Kubernetes does not garbage-collect, so it stayed `Bound` and the new
  StatefulSet re-bound the same Longhorn volume
  (`pvc-0acd3510-43ff-438c-8a54-c9fa8f310298`, 18d old).
- **Credentials intact** — and only because this repo had already disabled the
  chart's Secret objects. Chart-managed Secrets would have been deleted.
- **Meilisearch index lost.** Its PVC was a plain Helm-owned PVC. A fresh 1Gi
  volume was created; karakeep needs a reindex to restore search. Bookmarks
  themselves are in the primary volume and were never at risk.
- Verified after restore: 3/3 pods Running, `/api/health` 200,
  `karakeep-ash4d-tls` still valid to 2026-10-09.

karakeep is now running **unmanaged again**, exactly as before this session.
Re-adopting it requires resolving the field-ownership conflict first — see the
`kubectl diff` watch-out for why neither `helm.force` nor `managedFields` surgery
is free on a StatefulSet with an immutable `volumeClaimTemplates`.

**Why cert-manager was held.** It was next in line and is fully built and
pre-flighted, but it owns the six cert-manager CRDs and is a pre-existing Helm
release — the same profile as karakeep. Having just demonstrated that (a) SSA
conflicts are not visible to `kubectl diff` and (b) backing a path out uninstalls
the release, adopting it would have risked deleting every `Certificate`,
`Issuer` and `Order` in the cluster. Do the server-side dry-run pre-flight first.

pre-flight, which remains accurate.

karakeep is running unmanaged again, exactly as before this session.

My error was trusting the repo's own documented rollback ("remove the path"). That advice is safe for bundles Fleet never took ownership of, and lethal once it has. I should have used `spec.paused`. That's now corrected in the docs.

## What is adopted and healthy

All 17 BundleDeployments `ready=true, nonModified=true`, no GitRepo stalled:

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `lab-nemoclaw` | no-op first sync, zero restarts as predicted |
| `lab-ash4d-origin` | pod UID + startTime unchanged |
| `lab-openshell` | pod unchanged; adopted existing release rev 3→4 |
| `lab-buzz` (+minio) | all 4 pods byte-identical to pre-adoption |
| `lab-lab-memory` | raw path only (MCP servers, cronjob, cert) |
| `09-mcp/ollama-code` | migrated to `ai`, old namespace deleted, cert reissued |

Two PRs merged: [#5](https://github.com/darthzen/lab-fleet/pull/5) (the bundles) and [#6](https://github.com/darthzen/lab-fleet/pull/6) (corrections). `main` protected, so both went via PR rather than direct push.

## Three repo assumptions that were wrong

1. **"Roll back by removing the path" uninstalls an owned Helm release.** Cost me karakeep.
2. **`kubectl diff` clean does not predict Fleet.** Fleet applies server-side and needs field *ownership*. karakeep's conflicts were on fields whose values were semantically identical — live `cpu: 1` vs rendered `1000m`, live omitting `hostIPC` where the chart renders explicit `false`. `kubectl diff` normalizes exactly those away. Pre-flight with `kubectl apply --server-side --dry-run=server`.
3. **A nested path is not a staging gate.** Fleet deploys `<path>/<child>` the moment `<path>` is adopted. All three of `09-mcp/ollama-code`, `17-buzz/minio` and `18-lab-memory/raw` came up uninvited. Gating only works between siblings.

Also found and fixed: buzz reported `Modified` forever because the redis subchart sets `maxUnavailable`, which this cluster's API server silently strips (`MaxUnavailableStatefulSet` gate is off). Fleet could never converge. Now `Ready`, with no pod roll.

## Two things I deliberately did not do

**cert-manager is built and pre-flighted but not adopted.** It's a pre-existing Helm release owning 6 CRDs — the same profile as karakeep. Having just proven that SSA conflicts are invisible to `kubectl diff` and that backing out a path uninstalls, adopting it risked deleting every `Certificate`, `Issuer` and `Order` in the cluster. Its values do carry a real find: two DNS-01 args that exist only on the live object, whose absence would fail every renewal weeks later.

**Harbor/`registry` excluded.** Its objects are Helm-labelled but *ownerless* — no release secret, so the chart can't be recovered the way buzz and openshell were. It also serves the image an already-adopted path pulls.

input.content:
# Fleet bundle — Buzz relay (Helm).
#
# Nostr-based messaging relay at buzz.ash4d.com: one relay binary serving
# WebSocket + REST + web UI, backed by bundled PostgreSQL and Redis subcharts.
#
# Chart pinned to 0.1.6, matching the running release, so Fleet adopts rather
# than upgrades. Verified: renders byte-identical to live.
#
# The chart lives at oci://ghcr.io/block/buzz/charts/buzz — note the `/charts/`
# path segment. This bundle briefly vendored a copy of the chart recovered from
# the live Helm release secret, on the mistaken conclusion that 0.1.6 was
# unpublished. It is published; the earlier check probed
# oci://ghcr.io/block/buzz (no `/charts/`) and got a 404. The correct ref was
# recorded all along in this directory's values.yaml header and in shell history.
# The recovered copy rendered identically to what upstream serves, so nothing was
# wrong with the output — only with vendoring ~36 files that did not need to be
# in this repo. Lesson recorded in FLEET-WIRING.md: before concluding a chart is
# lost, pull the exact ref from the install command, not a guessed one.
#
# `github.com/block/buzz` is an unrelated audio-transcription desktop app, which
# is a red herring — the chart's own `home:`/`sources:` URLs point at it.
#
# Subcharts (postgres, redis from oci://registry-1.docker.io/cloudpirates) come
# from the published chart's own Chart.lock, so there is nothing to vendor and no
# `helm dependency build` for Fleet to run.
#
# PREREQUISITE SECRET: `buzz-relay` must exist in the namespace before this
# path is enabled. values.yaml sets secrets.existingSecret, which suppresses
# the chart's own Secret; the Postgres and Redis subcharts still read
# postgres-password / redis-password from that same name. See the buzz-relay
# repo's secret.md for the full required key list.
#
# TLS: there is deliberately NO tls block and NO cert-manager Certificate for
# buzz.ash4d.com on this cluster. TLS terminates at a GCP edge proxy, and both
# clusters run a Cloudflare DNS-01 solver against the same zone — if both
# issued for this host they would race on the same _acme-challenge TXT record
# at renewal time, unattended. Exactly one cluster owns that cert and it is
# GCP. This is why buzz-ext-ash4d-tls is a hand-made Secret here rather than a
# cert-manager Certificate. Do not "fix" this by adding an issuer annotation.
#
# The image is pinned by digest, split across image.repository and image.tag
# because the chart's helper does printf "%s:%s". The current pin is a
# SECURITY floor, not just a version choice: it is the first build containing
# the nostr 0.44.6 bump for RUSTSEC-2026-0216 (NIP-44 remote DoS). Do not roll
# back below it — see the comments in values.yaml.
#
# NOT vendored from the buzz-relay repo: gcp-proxy.yaml and gcp-ollama.yaml.
# Those are applied to a DIFFERENT cluster (the GCP k3s instance), not this
# one, so they are not lab-fleet's cluster state.
defaultNamespace: buzz
helm:
  releaseName: buzz
  chart: oci://ghcr.io/block/buzz/charts/buzz

Fleet pulled the OCI chart cleanly — `ready=true, nonModified=true`, and buzz's pods are still byte-identical to pre-adoption.

## What I found

**karakeep** — the exact installer, and it was in the `lab-memory` repo rather than Dropbox: `deploy/install.sh`.

```bash
helm repo add karakeep-app https://karakeep-app.github.io/helm-charts
helm upgrade --install karakeep karakeep-app/karakeep -n lab-memory \
  -f deploy/values.yaml \
  --set applicationSecretKey="$NEXTAUTH_SECRET" \
  --set meilisearchMasterKey="$MEILI_MASTER_KEY" \
  --wait --timeout 10m
```

The script's own comment says it pins those secrets because "the chart regenerates random secrets on every upgrade if these are not pinned" — the same trap I'd worked around independently.

**⚠️ `deploy/secrets.env` no longer exists.** Those credentials now live *only* in the two cluster Secrets. That reframes yesterday's uninstall from "recovered fully" to a near-miss: had they been chart-managed they'd have been deleted, and unrecoverable — sessions dead, Meilisearch permanently locked out with no way to reproduce the key. Worth backing up `lab-memory/karakeep` and `lab-memory/karakeep-meilesearch`. Note `~/Developer` symlinks into iCloud, so recreating `secrets.env` there syncs credentials to iCloud — that's a separate decision from git safety (it *is* gitignored).

**cert-manager** — recovered from a `lab-capture/lab-state-20260704-121209/` snapshot in the portfolio, which is a full `helm get values` dump of every release:

```bash
helm install cert-manager jetstack/cert-manager --version v1.20.2 \
  -n cert-manager --set crds.enabled=true
```

That's the whole thing, and it **independently confirms the DNS-01 watch-out**: the snapshot records `extraArgs: []`, and the live Deployment that day carried only five container args. So those two flags never came through Helm at any revision — `15-cert-manager/values.yaml` is the only place they're written down.

**Harbor** — nothing, anywhere. Only consumer-side references (`registry.ash4d.com`, robot accounts, the `harbor-push`/`harbor-pull` Secrets). The snapshot predates the `registry` namespace by about a week. That matches the cluster exactly: Helm-labelled, no release Secret. It stays unreconstructed.

## Your shell history caught a real mistake of mine

It contained `helm upgrade --install buzz oci://ghcr.io/block/buzz/charts/buzz`. **I was wrong that buzz's chart was unpublished** — I probed `oci://ghcr.io/block/buzz` without the `/charts/` segment, got a 404, and vendored 41 files on that basis. The correct ref was sitting in `17-buzz/values.yaml`'s own header the whole time; I read that file and didn't act on it.

Fixed in [#7](https://github.com/darthzen/lab-fleet/pull/7): buzz now references the immutable `0.1.6` upstream, matching what 04/05/06 already do. Verified byte-identical to both the recovered copy and live, and Fleet re-synced with no pod change.

Checking openshell rather than assume: it **does** publish immutable tags (`0.0.37`–`0.0.42`, plus content-addressed `0.0.0-dev.<sha>`), so my "no immutable version to pin" claim was wrong too. It still has to stay vendored, for a narrower reason — the running release came from the floating `0.0.0-dev` tag and none of the semvers reproduces it (8 objects vs live's 10). Un-vendoring means finding the matching `0.0.0-dev.<sha>` among ~90 candidates.

## Bonus: karakeep re-adoption is now unblocked

I ran the SSA pre-flight I'd only written down. Dry-run only, nothing changed:

- The plain SSA dry-run reproduces all 14 conflicts against manager `helm`.
- Adding `--force-conflicts` **succeeds on all 10 objects**, including the StatefulSet — so the API server doesn't reject it, and `volumeClaimTemplates` isn't actually being changed (live and rendered are semantically identical; live just carries defaulted `apiVersion`/`kind`/`volumeMode`).
- Fleet's field manager is **`fleetagent`**, confirmed from `managedFields` on the adopted buzz Deployment — where `helm` and `fleetagent` coexist precisely because that render matched live exactly.

So the unblock is a one-time ownership handoff before adopting, documented in `FLEET-WIRING.md`. Expect the karakeep and chrome pods to roll. I did **not** run it — after yesterday's incident that deserves a deliberate start, with the Secrets backed up first.

content.text:
Recreated at `~/Developer/lab-memory/deploy/secrets.env`.

- Both values read from the live Secrets and **digest-verified to match** — I never printed them
- Lengths 48 and 47, consistent with `install.sh`'s `openssl rand -base64 36` generation
- `chmod 600`, written under `umask 077`, and I refused to overwrite if it already existed
- Gitignored at `deploy/.gitignore:1`, confirmed invisible to `git status`
- Charset is base64-only, so `install.sh`'s `source` won't break on it, and its non-empty guard passes
- Cluster untouched: karakeep 3/3 Running, both Secret `resourceVersion`s unchanged (`9166842`/`9166843`)

As you accepted, this does sync to iCloud via the `~/Developer` symlink. The tradeoff went the right way — the alternative was a single copy existing only inside the cluster, which is what made yesterday's uninstall a near-miss.

## One thing to know before you ever run install.sh again

It reads the **lab-memory repo's** `deploy/values.yaml`, not lab-fleet's `18-lab-memory/values.yaml`, and those two have diverged:

1. It still carries the stale `OLLAMA_BASE_URL: http://192.168.7.153:11434`, so running it would revert karakeep off the in-cluster `ollama-exporter:9401` proxy — undoing one of the drift fixes.
2. It leaves the chart's Secret objects enabled, making both credentials Helm-owned again. That re-arms the exact deletion path that cost the Meilisearch index — recoverable now, but still worth avoiding.

Both recorded in `FLEET-WIRING.md` ([#8](https://github.com/darthzen/lab-fleet/pull/8) merged, `main` at `abd5227`, tree clean). Worth syncing that stale `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` into the lab-memory repo so the two can't disagree — say the word and I'll do it.

Still outstanding from earlier: the Meilisearch reindex, cert-manager held pending the SSA pre-flight, and the `GITREPO_SYNC_PERIOD=2h` polling gap.
